subject: Compute provisioning pathway for Vela Therapeutics — min GPUs & staged cadence
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@vela-therapeutics.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@vela-therapeutics.com>
Date: 2027-12-02T09:18:00Z
Subject: Compute provisioning options for our inference rollout

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We scoped our initial rollout internally and wanted to surface a few constraints so you can propose a concrete provisioning path: 

- Target models: open LLMs (13B and 70B variants) for both chat and batch scoring.
- Expected steady-state inference: ~6M tokens/day initially, peaking to ~25M tokens/day within 3 months.
- Latency SLO: 95p < 250ms for single-turn chat.
- Burst behavior: spikes up to 3x baseline during daytime experiments.
- Compliance: production must run in us-west and keep audit logs for 12 months.

Can you outline 2–3 compute allocation options that map to: (a) starting cluster size (min GPUs), (b) a 3-month ramp cadence, (c) burst handling approach (hot lanes vs. autoscale), and (d) any recommended prewarm/canary steps? Prefer a short table and a recommended path.

Samir will be the internal infra lead on our side — feel free to loop him in.

Cheers,
Alice

--
Alice Chen
Head of ML Platforms | Vela Therapeutics
alice.chen@vela-therapeutics.com

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Compute provisioning options for our inference rollout

Hi Alice — great summary, thanks. Attached is a short capacity slate (vela_capacity_slate_v1.pdf) plus an editable MAP workbook. Below are three pragmatic pathways we typically recommend based on similar deals; I highlight which one matches your stated constraints best.

Quick summary table (tokens/day -> suggested start / min GPUs -> 3-month cadence):

1) Light onramp (conservative)
- Start: 8x A10-equivalent GPUs (min 8 GPUs dedicated)
- Month 1 → Month 3: 8 → 16 GPUs (scale by usage triggers)
- Burst: autoscale to shared burst pool (best-effort), optional hot lane for priority requests
- When to pick: if you prioritize cost containment and can tolerate slower warm-up.

2) Balanced (recommended)
- Start: 16x A100-equivalent GPUs (min 16 GPUs dedicated)
- Month 1 → Month 3: 16 → 40 GPUs (phased additions at weeks 4 and 8)
- Burst: reserved hot lane (10 GPU hot lane) + autoscale fallback to hosted burst pool
- Why recommended: meets 25M tokens/day growth with margin for 3x spikes while keeping predictable performance and room to canary model variants.

3) Aggressive (throughput-first)
- Start: 48x A100-equivalent GPUs (min 48 GPUs dedicated)
- Month 1 → Month 3: 48 → 80 GPUs (fast ramp if adoption is immediate)
- Burst: larger dedicated hot lanes + preprovisioned reserved capacity for experiments
- When to pick: enterprise-grade SLOs with immediate heavy usage.

Prewarm/canary notes: we recommend a 2-week canary (2–3 GPUs) running representative prompts, then a staged canary at 10% traffic routing for 72 hours prior to full switch. Prewarming KV caches for target model prompts reduces first-token latency.

Operational bits:
- Region: us-west deployment for dedicated cluster + cross-region failover to us-east for disaster recovery.
- Observability: we’ll provide per-route token latency + cost dashboards and alerts for token-rate anomalies.

Next steps: we can turn the Balanced path into a committed Dedicated proposal. If you want, I can loop legal/procurement and a pricing deck. DocuSign ready once you confirm the path.

Regards,
Markus Klein

Thanks,
Markus

Subject: Re: Compute provisioning options for our inference rollout — recommended path and next steps

Alice / Samir — thanks for the prompt follow-ups. Per internal checks, here are concise answers and a recommended next step.

Answers to Samir’s questions:
1) Performance delta (70B profile, representative prompt set):
- A100-equivalent (our infra): ~2.8x tokens/sec vs A10-equivalent in throughput tests. 95p latency: ~140–180ms on A100 vs ~320–380ms on A10 for same sequence lengths. (Bench summary attached in the capacity slate.)
2) Hot lane design:
- Implementation: we provision a 10 GPU hot lane as reserved, non-preemptible instances within the same dedicated cluster (QoS reserved). This keeps locality benefits (shared KV cache) and predictable latency. Autoscale fallback routes to our hosted burst pool (best-effort) when reserved hot lane saturates — we throttle and signal backpressure to callers.
3) Pricing / commitment trade-offs:
- 6-month trial: shorter financial commitment, smaller onboarding credits, standard SLA. Recommended if you want to validate traffic patterns first.
- 12-month commit: 10% discount on committed units, larger onboarding credit (~2 weeks free runtime) and SLA uplift (response time / credits). Also simplifies long-term capacity planning and reduces unit cost.

Recommended path (formal proposal next):
- Start: Balanced path (16 A100-equivalent GPUs dedicated)
- Min GPUs (hard floor): 16 GPUs committed for Month 0–1
- Ramp schedule: Week 4 add 8 GPUs (to 24), Week 8 add 16 GPUs (to 40), review metrics at week 12 for additional scaling.
- Hot lane: 10 GPUs reserved, same cluster, non-preemptible. Autoscale fallback to hosted burst pool.
- Canary: 2-week functional canary, 72h traffic canary at 10% before full cutover.

Next steps: I’ve attached a proposed MAP (vela_mutual_action_plan.xlsx) and a capacity slate. If Vela agrees to the Balanced + 12mo commit path, I’ll circulate a term sheet and DocuSign link (we have VELA-2027-09 preseeded). If you prefer the 6m trial we’ll prepare a trial contract variant.

Please reply with which commitment you prefer and we’ll advance legal/procurement.

Best,
